## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- Only community sources confirm the wave size this break works in.
- Only community sources confirm the best tide.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind conflict now leans clearly to the profile: four readable sources give southeast (135 deg) as the best or offshore wind (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, LMBK Surf House); only Surf-Forecast's template says east-northeast (67.5 deg). Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, DHM) and S-SW (LMBK), all near the profile's 205-235 optimum. Size: WannaSurf starts at 5-6 ft and holds 8 ft+, Indonesian Surf Guide gives head high to double overhead (about 6-12 ft faces), DHM gives 4-6 ft Hawaiian as optimal (about 8-12 ft faces); the profile's 12 ft maximum is now supported, but its 4 ft minimum is below every source's starting size (5-6 ft). Period: LMBK says swells under 14 s struggle to wrap into the bay, which supports the profile's 14 s minimum; nothing supports the 17 s ideal. Tide is still split: low tide (WannaSurf 'Low tide only', rising; Indonesian Surf Guide 'best at low tide') versus mid-incoming (DHM: 'dangerously shallow at low tide and closes out at high tide'); WannaSurf's own text also warns 'Watch out for low tide sessions!!'. The profile's low_to_mid covers both readings. Season: May-September (LMBK, DHM) or May-October (Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide). Consistency conflict: Surf-Forecast's template says 'quite reliable surf' while WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, LMBK and The Inertia call it fickle or inconsistent. Independence caveat: the new sources are mostly surf-camp or directory sites, and Indonesian Surf Guide's page promotes LMBK Surf House. Dated sources: The Inertia 2023, indonesia.travel 2025, Indonesian Surf Guide 2025, LMBK 2026, DHM 2026; Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf are undated. Surfer Today still returns 403 and is kept from search evidence. No peer-reviewed, survey or official source was found (Crossref searches returned nothing on this break).

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 5–6 ft | documented | S2 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | hawaiian scale: 4–6 ft; relative face: head high to double overhead · mixed (see value) | documented | S6, S8 | no separate setting; working range 4–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 8 ft | documented | S2 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.5-2 m / 5-6 ft (the page's own conversion; face or offshore height not stated); no other excerpt gives a minimum.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+”
- **Ideal range**: DHM Surf Camp says 4-6 ft Hawaiian scale is optimal and the Indonesian Surf Guide gives head high to double overhead (a face height relative to the surfer); neither source converts its scale to face feet, so no conversion is applied.
  - S8 (DHM Surf Camp (dhm.co.id)): “Swell size of 4 to 6 feet (Hawaiian scale) is optimal.”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Wave size | Head high to double overhead”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 2.5 m+ / 8 ft+, an open-ended bound (scale not stated); no excerpt gives a true upper limit.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Starts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+”

### Swell period

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |

| Ideal | big (substantial) groundswell | documented | S1, S3, S6, S8 | `ideal_swell_period_s` 17 s |

Notes:

- **Ideal**: Surfer Today (search summary) says it needs big groundswells, the Indonesian Surf Guide a substantial SW groundswell and DHM southwest groundswell, and Surf-Forecast says it tends to receive distant groundswells; no ideal period in seconds is given.
  - S3 (Surfer Today): “Desert Point is a left-hand reef break that needs big ground swells to work.”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “demanding a substantial SW groundswell”
  - S8 (DHM Surf Camp (dhm.co.id)): “The wave requires southwest groundswell”
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “Tends to receive distant groundswells”
- **Acceptable**: LMBK Surf House says anything below 14 seconds will likely struggle to wrap into the bay, so 14 s is the stated lower bound; no upper bound is given.
  - S7 (LMBK Surf House): “Anything below 14 seconds will likely struggle to wrap into the bay.”
- **Short-period behaviour**: LMBK Surf House's statement about periods under 14 s.
  - S7 (LMBK Surf House): “Anything below 14 seconds will likely struggle to wrap into the bay.”
- **Long-period behaviour**: No excerpt describes how the break handles long-period swell beyond preferring it.

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast (ideal), WannaSurf (good), the Indonesian Surf Guide (best) and DHM (required) all say southwest, and LMBK says a large south to southwest swell is best; SW = 225 deg.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest.”
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionSouthWest”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Swell Direction: Southwest (SW) swells provide the best setup.”
  - S8 (DHM Surf Camp (dhm.co.id)): “The wave requires southwest groundswell”
  - S7 (LMBK Surf House): “Best Swell Direction | Large South – Southwest Swell”
- **Acceptable range**: No excerpt gives a working window; the widest statement is LMBK's best direction, south to southwest.
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break with quite reliable surf, while WannaSurf calls it one of the most inconsistent waves in the world needing a mega swell and The Inertia, LMBK (3/10) and the Indonesian Surf Guide call it fickle.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf”
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Very long, hollow waves that almost always end in a barrel...one of the most inconsistent waves in the world, needing a mega swell”
  - S4 (The Inertia): “It's a fickle beast, but under the right conditions, it can provide long left-hand barrels”
  - S7 (LMBK Surf House): “Consistency | 3/10 (Fickle: needs a “Code Red” swell pulse)”
  - S6 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “the wave can peel flawlessly for up to 300 meters...Desert Point is notoriously fickle”

  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Best tide positionLow tide only...Best tide movementRising tide”

- **Rising or falling**: WannaSurf gives the best tide movement as rising and DHM calls mid-incoming the golden window.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Best tide positionLow tide only...Best tide movementRising tide”

- **Local tide data**: App tide data, not research evidence: data/tide_stations.json links this spot to the EOT20 global tide model cell eot20:desert-point (datum model mean sea level), 5.3 km from the break, as primary (looked in data/tide_stations.json, data/tides/constants_eot20.json and docs/tides.md); the app shows predicted astronomical tides only; catalog caveat: In the Lombok Strait, where tides and tidal streams are complex; the 1/8 degree model is less reliable here than on an open coast.

## Conflicting information

- **Wind · offshore**: WannaSurf gives southeast as the good wind and the Indonesian Surf Guide and LMBK call southeast the ideal or best offshore wind (135 deg), while Surf-Forecast says the ideal winds are from the east-northeast (67.5 deg).
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WannaSurf says low tide only and the Indonesian Surf Guide says it performs best at low tide (more critical as the tide drops), while DHM says it breaks dangerously shallow at low tide, closes out at high tide, and that mid-incoming is the golden window.
